title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus reshapes the rhizosphere microbiome of alfalfa in response to above‐ground attack by aphids and a fungal plant pathogen
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Plants assemble beneficial rhizosphere microbiomes through a ‘cry for help’ mechanism upon pathogen or insect herbivore attack. The arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) can influence the composition of microbial communities in the plant rhizosphere. However, their impacts on the rhizosphere microbiome in response to co-attacks of pathogens and insect herbivores remain unknown. In this study, a mesocosm of alfalfa, Rhizophagus intraradices, Phoma medicaginis and Acyrthosiphon pisum was used to elucidate how AMF alter the plant rhizosphere microbiome and its responses to multiple biotic stresses. The AMF significantly increased the activity of soil acid phosphatase, urease and β-glucosidase, causing an enhanced absorption of soil phosphorus by plants. The soil enzymes were also significantly and positively correlated with plant shoot properties, including polyphenol oxidase and peroxidase, salicylic acid (SA) and trypsin inhibitor (TI). Although all the AMF, P. medicaginis and aphids altered the rhizosphere microbiome of alfalfa, the AMF recruited beneficial microorganisms in the alfalfa rhizosphere in response to pathogens and aphid attacks. The multi-interaction also increased the complexity and stability of the rhizosphere microbial network. Additionally, there is a significant correlation between soil enzyme activity, nitrate nitrogen, TI, SA, biomass, disease severity and the rhizosphere microbiome. Therefore, the AMF improves plant defence and soil biochemistry profiles and assists alfalfa in assembling beneficial rhizosphere microbiomes in response to P. medicaginis and aphid attacks. These findings are vital for understanding the interactions between transboundary species in above- and below-ground systems altered by AMF in natural ecosystems.

摘要

植物在受到病原菌或食草昆虫侵袭时，会通过“求救”机制聚集有益的根际微生物群落。丛枝菌根真菌(AMF)可以影响植物根际微生物群落的组成。然而，AMF在病原菌和食草昆虫共同侵袭时对根际微生物群落的影响仍不清楚。 本研究以紫花苜蓿、根内根孢囊霉(Rhizophagus intraradices)、苜蓿茎点霉 (Phoma medicaginis)和豌豆蚜(Acyrthosiphon pisum)组成的试验系统为基础，阐明了AMF如何改变植物根际微生物群落及其对多种生物胁迫的响应。 研究结果表明:AMF显著提高了土壤酸性磷酸酶、脲酶和β-葡萄糖苷酶的活性，从而增强了植物对土壤磷的吸收。土壤酶与植物地上部生理指标呈显著正相关，包括多酚氧化酶和过氧化物酶、水杨酸和胰蛋白酶抑制剂。AMF、苜蓿茎点霉和蚜虫改变了苜蓿的根际微生物组，但AMF为应对病原菌和蚜虫的侵袭，在病虫害发生后在苜蓿根际招募了有益微生物。这种多重相互作用也增加了根际微生物网络的复杂性和稳定性。此外，土壤酶活性、硝态氮、水杨酸、胰蛋白酶抑制剂、生物量、病害严重度和根际微生物组之间存在显著相关性。 综上所述，AMF可改善植物的防御能力和土壤生化状况，并帮助苜蓿在应对苜蓿茎点霉和蚜虫侵袭时组建有益的根际微生物组。这些发现对于理解自然生态系统中AMF调控地上和地下系统中跨界物种之间的相互作用至关重要。
